Or you can take a more structured approach in the form of a longer conversation. Use open-ended questions that encourage honest input and help surface where your impact is most visible. Here are some examples:

或者你可以采取更结构化的方式，进行一次更长的对话。用开放式问题鼓励诚实的输入，帮你看清你的影响在哪里最可见。下面是一些例子：

  • What kind of impact do you think I've had on the team as a tech lead?你觉得我作为技术负责人，对团队产生了什么样的影响？
  • How well do you think that impact aligns with what you expect from someone in this role?你觉得这种影响与你对这个角色的期待吻合得如何？
  • What are the areas where you feel I didn't contribute as much as I could have?在哪些领域你觉得我本可以贡献更多，却没有？
  • What would you suggest I focus on to improve?你建议我聚焦什么来提升？
  • What should I start doing differently?我应该开始在哪些方面换种做法？
  • How would you describe your experience working alongside me?你会如何描述与我一起工作的体验？
  • What should I be focusing on right now that I may be overlooking?有什么我现在应该聚焦、却可能忽略了的？
— PDF p.351 —

Whenever possible, tie these questions back to the goals you've set. For example, if your focus is on improving collaboration, you might ask: "How effective do you think I've been in bringing people together to solve problems?"

只要可能，把这些问题与你设定的目标挂钩。比如，如果你的焦点是改善协作，你可以问："你觉得我在把大家聚到一起解决问题方面，做得有多有效？"

The key step is to track this feedback. Make it a habit to write down what you hear, including who said it, when, and in what context (e.g., during a critical incident, a big release, or a high-stakes delivery). Keeping this kind of record helps you identify patterns, document impact, and, most importantly, prove your value as a tech lead. When it comes time for performance discussions, this evidence will help you clearly articulate the influence you've had—not just what you did but the outcomes your leadership helped create.

关键步骤是追踪这些反馈。把你听到的内容写下来——包括谁说的、什么时候、在什么上下文里（比如一次关键事故、一次大发布、或一次高风险交付）——让它成为习惯。保持这种记录帮你识别模式、记录影响，最重要的是，证明你作为技术负责人的价值。当绩效讨论到来时，这些证据会帮你清晰地表达你所产生的影响——不只是你做了什么，而是你的领导力帮助创造了什么结果。

Another powerful metric to assess your effectiveness as a tech lead is overall team performance. When the team is performing well, shipping high-quality work, collaborating effectively, and growing in confidence, it's a clear sign of strong leadership. On the other hand, if the team is struggling, it's often a reflection of gaps in leadership, support, or clarity. That's why it's essential to continuously assess not just your individual impact but your team's performance as a whole. There are structured ways to evaluate how well your team is functioning. You can explore those in the section "How to Evaluate If Your Team Is High-Performing" on page 195.

另一个评估你作为技术负责人效能的强力指标，是团队的整体表现。当团队表现良好、交付高质量工作、有效协作、信心不断增长时，这是强领导力的明确信号。反过来，如果团队在挣扎，往往反映出在领导力、支持或清晰性上的缺口。这就是为什么不仅要持续评估你个人的影响，还要评估团队整体表现。有结构化的方式来评估团队运作得如何。你可以在第 195 页"如何评估你的团队是否高绩效"一节中探索这些方式。

Whether sprint demos or milestone reviews, your showcase rituals are simple, visible signals of team effectiveness. These sessions are more than routine ceremonies; they provide a track record of your team's results and outcomes.

无论是迭代演示还是里程碑评审，你的展示仪式都是团队效能简单而可见的信号。这些环节不只是例行公事；它们提供了一份关于团队成果与产出的履历。

Are you consistently demonstrating progress? Is the work tied clearly to business value? Regular, high-quality showcases reflect alignment, focus, and momentum, all of which point back to strong technical leadership.

你是否在持续展示进展？工作是否与业务价值清晰挂钩？定期、高质量的展示反映出对齐、聚焦和动能——所有这些都指向强大的技术领导力。

Another great question to ask yourself is this: how is your team doing when you are not there? It's actually a sign of great leadership if your team is properly functioning even in your absence. A team that can operate effectively without your constant presence is a strong indicator that you've empowered them well.

另一个值得问自己的好问题是：你不在场时，你的团队表现如何？如果你的团队在你不在的情况下仍能正常运作，这其实是伟大领导力的标志。一支没有你持续在场也能有效运转的团队，是一个强指标——说明你很好地赋能了他们。

Understanding your own impact, and helping others understand it too, allows you to focus your energy where it matters, advocate for the recognition you deserve, and grow with confidence in your leadership journey.

理解你自己的影响，并帮助别人也理解它，能让你把精力聚焦在真正重要的地方、为你应得的认可发声，并在你的领导力之旅中自信地成长。

Balancing the Demands of Tech Leadership to Avoid Burnout平衡技术领导力的多重要求以避免 burnout

A common trap tech leads fall into is trying to manage it all at the same time. We think we can do it all: write code, lead people, align stakeholders, and handle operations. But without clear boundaries or balance, this can quickly lead to burnout. You may find yourself working late to catch up on what didn't get done during the day or constantly switching contexts, never fully present in one mode or the other.

技术负责人常掉进的一个陷阱，是试图同时管理一切。我们以为自己什么都能做：写代码、带人、对齐干系人、处理运营。但没有清晰边界或平衡，这很快就会导致 burnout。你可能发现自己在加班补白天没做完的事，或者不停地切换上下文，永远无法完全投入某一种模式。

I often hear tech leads say, "All my real work happens outside of working hours because I'm always trapped in meetings." But those meetings are real work, and they are often harder than any technical task. They're where alignment happens, risks get surfaced, and relationships are built.

我常听到技术负责人说："我所有真正的工作都发生在下班时间，因为我整天被困在会议里。"但那些会议就是真正的工作，而且它们往往比任何技术任务都更难。对齐在那里发生、风险在那里被暴露、关系在那里被建立。

Still, it's an antipattern for tech leads to spend all their time in meetings. Not every meeting needs you. Protecting time for deep work, team connection, and strategic thinking is essential. Delegate when you can. Push back on meetings where your presence isn't adding value. Block focus time, and treat it like you would any other critical commitment.

尽管如此，技术负责人把所有时间都花在会议上是一种反模式。不是每个会议都需要你。保护用于深度工作、团队连接和战略思考的时间至关重要。能委派就委派。对你出席不带来价值的会议要推回去。锁定专注时间，并像对待任何其他关键承诺一样对待它。

Constantly trying to be everywhere is how that pressure builds, and it slowly leads to exhaustion. Some people notice the signs early. I didn't.

不断试图无处不在，压力就是这样积累起来的，并缓慢地导向耗竭。有些人很早就注意到信号，我没有。

Just five weeks into my first tech lead role, I experienced facial paralysis. I basically couldn't move the right side of my face. I felt bad for my team and for myself. And yet, I took only a couple of days off, even though recovery typically takes months.

在我担任第一个技术负责人角色仅仅五周时，我出现了面瘫。我基本上没法动右半边脸。我为团队、也为自己感到难过。然而，我只休息了几天——尽管恢复通常需要几个月。

I came back to work taking strong medication and wearing sunglasses for weeks so people wouldn't see I couldn't fully close my eye. I even joked about it.

我回来上班时服用着强效药物，戴了好几周墨镜，好让别人看不出我没法完全闭上那只眼睛。我甚至拿它开玩笑。

At the time, I thought I was doing the right thing, pushing through, showing strength. But in truth, I was afraid. Afraid of disappointing people, of being seen

当时我以为自己在做对的事——硬扛过去、展现坚强。但实际上，我是害怕。害怕让别人失望、害怕被看作

— PDF p.352 —

as weak, of not rising to the challenge. I also realized I saw myself as a bottleneck for my team; I didn't trust them to handle things alone.

软弱、害怕没能迎接挑战。我也意识到，我把自己看成了团队的瓶颈；我不信任他们能独自处理事情。

I've thought a lot about the message that was sent. I told myself I was being committed, but what I really modeled was self-neglect. I normalized working through serious health issues, and I made it harder for others to feel safe prioritizing their own well-being. That's not the kind of leader I want to be.

我反复思考这件事传递出去的信号。我告诉自己我在敬业，但我真正示范的是自我忽视。我把"带着严重健康问题硬扛工作"正常化了，也让别人更难安心地把自己的福祉放在优先位置。那不是我想成为的那种领导。

Despite ignoring the doctor's advice, I was lucky to recover quickly. But that doesn't mean the impact wasn't real. The stress lingered, and I lost trust in my ability to set healthy boundaries. It took me months to start integrating the lessons from that experience into how I lead.

尽管违背了医生的建议，我很幸运恢复得很快。但这并不意味着影响不真实。压力挥之不去，我也失去了对自己设立健康边界能力的信任。我花了好几个月，才开始把那次经历的教训融入我的领导方式中。

This is one of the reasons I wrote this book: to help others recognize these patterns earlier. No deadline, sprint, or meeting is more important than your health. Your team needs a leader who's well and who makes it safe for them to be human too.

这也是我写这本书的原因之一：帮别人更早地识别这些模式。没有任何截止日期、迭代或会议比你的健康更重要。你的团队需要一位状态良好的领导，一位让他们也能安心"做个正常人"的领导。

Since then, I've been more intentional about how I work and lead. Here are some strategies that have helped me and that might help you too:

从那以后，我在如何工作和如何领导上变得更有意识。下面是一些帮到我的策略，也许也能帮到你：

Keep yourself in check. Constantly.持续关照自己

How are you feeling? How are you managing it all? What do you need?

你感觉怎么样？你是怎么应对这一切的？你需要什么？

Ask people around you too. Sometimes we're so trapped in our own heads we miss the signs, but others notice. I remember when I wasn't feeling OK, I started getting more "How are you doing?" or "How's everything?" from people around me. It was like they could sense something.

也问问身边的人。有时候我们太困在自己的脑子里，错过了信号，但别人注意到了。我记得我状态不好的时候，身边的人开始更多地问"你怎么样？"或"一切还好吗？"好像他们能察觉到什么。

One time, a team member said in a one-on-one, "I feel like you're stressed. What's happening?" It caught me completely off guard; I thought I was hiding it well. Trust those cues.

有一次，一位团队成员在一对一里说："我感觉你压力很大。发生什么了？"这完全出乎我意料；我以为自己藏得很好。请相信那些信号。

Ask for help. Early.及早求助

The tech lead role can feel lonely, but you are not alone. Admitting you need support and accepting it is essential.

技术负责人这个角色可能让人感到孤独，但你并不孤单。承认你需要支持、并接受支持，是至关重要的。

Here's who I've leaned on: my manager, someone I could turn to for advice, direction, or just to listen; other tech leads, through internal groups or one-on-one chats that helped normalize challenges; a coach, someone objective to help me think things through; a mentor inside the company I met with regularly; and my team.

下面是我依靠过的人：我的经理——我可以向他寻求建议、方向，或只是找个人倾听；其他技术负责人——通过内部小组或一对一聊天，帮我把挑战正常化；一位教练——一个客观的人，帮我把事情想清楚；公司内部一位我定期见面的导师；以及我的团队。

When I admitted I was overwhelmed and showed them my to-do list, they volunteered to help. We found things they were interested in. That act empowered them and was a relief for me.

当我承认自己不堪重负、把待办清单给他们看时，他们主动提出帮忙。我们找到了他们感兴趣的事。这个举动赋能了他们，也让我松了一口气。

— PDF p.353 —

There is support around you. Sometimes, you just have to reach out.

支持就在你身边。有时候，你只需要伸手。

Take some time off.休个假

Many tech leads feel they can't take a vacation, that their team can't function without them. But if that's true, your team is too dependent on you. Great leadership means your team can perform even when you're not there.

很多技术负责人觉得自己不能休假，觉得团队没有自己就转不动。但如果真是这样，你的团队就过度依赖你了。伟大的领导力意味着：即使你不在，团队也能正常发挥。

Plan more living, not less working.规划更多生活，而不是更少工作

I saved my favorite strategy for last because it completely changed how I think about balance.

我把最喜欢的策略留到最后，因为它彻底改变了我对平衡的看法。

For a long time, I thought the key to avoiding burnout was working less. So I tried things like starting work later, shutting the laptop at 6 PM, or adding more breaks to my day. But the problem wasn't just the amount of work; it was what I wasn't doing outside of it.

很长一段时间里，我以为避免 burnout 的关键是少工作。所以我试过晚点开始工作、下午 6 点合上电脑、或在一天里加更多休息。但问题不只是工作量；问题在于我在工作之外没有在做什么。

When I stopped working, I found myself wondering: now what? I had no hobbies, no post-work plans, no clear way to transition out of work mode. That emptiness made it easier to just keep working, and harder to disconnect.

当我停下工作时，我发现自己在想：现在干嘛？我没有爱好、没有下班后的计划、没有清晰的方式从工作模式切换出来。那种空虚让"继续工作"变得更容易，也让"断开连接"变得更难。

Eventually, I realized I needed to plan life the same way I plan work. So I started doing more life. I began booking activities after work that I paid for in advance, giving myself skin in the game so I'd actually follow through. I made plans with friends, creating social commitments I didn't want to cancel. I picked up small personal projects, like building Lego sets or solving puzzles, that gave me the same sense of progress and momentum I enjoy at work. And I got a dog, which naturally forced me to take breaks and spend more time outside.

最终，我意识到我需要像规划工作一样规划生活。于是我开始"多做生活"。我开始预订下班后的活动、并且提前付钱，让自己真金白银地投入，好让自己真的会去。我和朋友约计划，制造我不想取消的社交承诺。我捡起一些小的个人项目——比如拼乐高、解谜——它们给我带来和工作中一样的进步感和动能。我还养了一只狗，它自然地迫使我休息、花更多时间在户外。

This is about making space for life to grow around it. If you want to sustain your energy and protect your well-being, schedule living with intention.

这是关于为生活腾出空间，让它在工作周围生长。如果你想持续保持能量、保护自己的福祉，就要有意识地为生活排日程。

Prioritizing your self-care means prioritizing your team's health too. They look to you for cues. If you overwork, they overwork. If you're stressed, they get stressed.

把自我关怀放在优先位置，也意味着把团队的健康放在优先位置。他们从你身上读信号。如果你过度工作，他们就过度工作。如果你压力大，他们也压力大。

If you're not well, you can't help anyone.

如果你状态不好，你谁也帮不了。

Key Takeaway本章要点

Technical leadership is rarely about having all the answers; really, it's about creating the conditions for your team to thrive. In this chapter, you've seen how

技术领导力很少在于拥有所有答案；真正的关键在于为你的团队创造绽放的条件。在本章中，你已经看到

— PDF p.354 —

that comes to life across the areas that matter most: developing talent, managing stakeholders, and bridging the gap between tech and business.

这一点如何在最重要的几个领域中落地：培养人才、管理干系人、以及弥合技术与业务之间的鸿沟。

Your job as a tech lead is part translator, part strategist, part coach. You guide technical direction, support the people around you, and navigate relationships that extend far beyond your team. Each decision you make—how you spend your time, how you communicate, how you support growth—sends a signal and shapes your team's culture.

作为技术负责人，你的工作一半是翻译者、一半是战略家、一半是教练。你指导技术方向、支持身边的人、并经营那些远远超出团队边界的关系。你做的每一个决定——如何花时间、如何沟通、如何支持成长——都在发出信号，并塑造你团队的文化。

Sustainable, effective leadership doesn't come from doing more. It comes from doing the right things, with clarity and intention. Start where you are. Pay attention to what's working. Ask for help when you need it.

可持续、有效的领导力不在于做得更多。它在于带着清晰和意图去做正确的事。从你所在的地方开始。留意什么在起作用。需要时就求助。

The most impactful tech leads aren't perfect; they're thoughtful, adaptable, and always learning.

最有影响力的技术负责人不是完美的；他们是深思熟虑的、适应力强的、并且始终在学习的。
